builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
summary: Replaces aggregate-outcome safety testing with a controlled paired executable protocol that isolates whether upstream messages change executor actions by freezing computation and varying delivery modes. Costs include implementation of deterministic policy states, preassigned budgets, and format-matched placebo construction, plus the need to run multiple paired scenarios rather than simple end-to-end evaluation. Can fail if applied to natural traffic without recognizing it measures constructed information dependencies, not natural failure rates, and results may not generalize across different message compositions or model behaviors.
rationale: This evaluation protocol provides actionable diagnostic capability for agent safety testing under constrained infrastructure, but requires validation that the constructed scenarios match production risks before adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces aggregate-outcome safety testing with a controlled paired executable protocol that isolates whether upstream messages change executor actions by freezing computation and varying delivery modes. Costs include implementation of deterministic policy states, preassigned budgets, and format-matched placebo construction, plus the need to run multiple paired scenarios rather than simple end-to-end evaluation. Can fail if applied to natural traffic without recognizing it measures constructed information dependencies, not natural failure rates, and results may not generalize across different message compositions or model behaviors.
Real delivery produces 21.4% risky-world violations versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery at N=4; real delivery improves safe completion by 74.2 points in a lookup-dependent regime.
